hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional local two-second prototype, not verified world safety. Metric depths, body sizes, road edges and residuals are model estimates. The forward crossing pedestrian and bus are visibly beyond the modeled 38 m road patch; the prototype expressly assumes their complete bodies remain outside it for two seconds. Right-side parking-lot vehicles and left-side sidewalk pedestrians are outside the local pavement domain and are conditionally assumed not to enter. Occluded entrants, parking departures and other unobserved traffic are excluded conditions, not demonstrated absent. The nearby passing BMW is retained with asynchronous alignment and two bounded motion variants. Initial ego speed is 8.5064 m/s; the lower desired speed is a deceleration preference, not an assertion that ego is already slow or stopped. No trajectory optimization or independent verification has been executed here.

premises.statement: Local domain is this finite continuous street-pavement patch only, including current ego footprint and approximately 17 m of expected forward travel. Adopt no new unobserved entrant into this domain during [0,2]. Observed parking-lot vehicles across the right sidewalk remain outside; sidewalk pedestrians remain outside; the distant crossing pedestrian, bus, work equipment and distant traffic remain wholly beyond x=38. These are falsifiable exclusions, not evidence of an empty world. The observed nearby passing BMW and five left-curb parked vehicles are explicitly modeled. Re-observation is required before extending this domain or horizon.

Adopt approximate passenger-vehicle and work-van dimensions as monocular scale priors. The white SUV is modeled as 4.9 m long and 1.95 m wide. In the reference front image its oblique front/body extent, the other parked bodies, road convergence and apparent wheel-contact heights support an approximately 22 m center distance with meter-scale residual, rather than certified depth. The right curb and left parking/curb frontage support street edges near y=-3.5 and y=9.2. The front view supports the forward patch; the rear image and trusted short ego history support continuity beneath and just behind ego. Longitudinal polygon edges are local modeling cuts, not detected physical barriers. Road uncertainty is 0.4 m; calibration supplies axes and perspective only, not a verified ground plane.

The five aligned left-curb vehicles are visually parked and conditionally remain parked for two seconds. Adopted modes use their full estimated stationary bodies. Reasonable adverse variants add 0.2 m per-side bounded pose/body-envelope spread, allowing small settling or creep but excluding departure, door opening and pulling into traffic. All variants contain the native t=0 body; additional monocular metric residual remains separate.

The dark BMW approaching in front history is observed passing close on the left in the back-left capture 0.064993 s before reference. Estimated native evidence center is [-1,4.1]; absolute westbound speed is conditionally 8–12 m/s, supported qualitatively by the approach/pass sequence. Across the capture-to-reference interval all retained modes have speed at most 12 m/s, displacement at most 0.8 m, and alignment residual 0.4 m. Reference center is estimated [-1.65,4.1]. For [0,2], adopted motion remains straight westbound at 8–11 m/s; adverse motion allows up to 12 m/s and center lateral displacement at most 0.15 m, with fixed yaw pi. No reversal or turn toward ego is adopted. Whole-interval rectangles include full 4.9 by 1.9 m bodies and outward numerical room; source residual 0.4 m is additional to alignment residual.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible white SUV in the left parked row has a conventional midsize-SUV body; 1.95 m is an adopted body-width prior, not measured ground truth.
Its visible front and oblique side are consistent with an approximately 4.9 m SUV; this matches the native body hypothesis.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: Use the white SUV's apparent frontal/oblique body extent, visible parked-row spacing, wheel-contact perspective and road-edge convergence jointly. Perspective foreshortening and unknown contact height preclude a unique solution; adopt its center near [22,7] m and propagate approximate scale to the adjacent parked row and street edges. Native actor residuals increase from 1.3 to 1.8 m along the row. The resulting road includes both travel directions and curbside pavement, not merely the ego lane. These estimates remain conditional on the explicit size and approximately continuous local-surface hypotheses.

capture.navigation_intent: Continue along the visible drivable road when permissible; obey visible signals and yield as needed. No map or future ego route is supplied.
